editorial.headline: Water Tourism Across Rivers, Reefs and Open Water
editorial.standfirst: This activity brings managed water-based recreation into one operating category, from rafting and diving to marina entertainment and sailing adventures.
editorial.body:
Water tourism under this activity is organised recreation built around rivers, the sea and related facilities in defined areas. On the river, it includes the management of white-water rafting as a principal activity, alongside rafting tubing, river boarding, canoeing, kayaking and body-rafting experiences. The marine side is equally broad: diving activities, snorkelling, free diving and sea walking sit alongside the sale, rental and repair of diving equipment and the organisation of dive travel at local, national and international scale.

The scope also reaches beyond an individual excursion. Operators may run activities connected with marine and coastal environmental care, as well as comparable work supporting environmental preservation within a particular area. Marina-related entertainment and recreation are included, as are managed water-tourism activities such as windsurfing, parasailing, jet skiing, motor boating, sailing, surfing, rafting, traditional or dragon-boat racing, boating adventures, sail-training adventures, tourist submarine experiences and flying boards. These principal activities may be supported by facilities, including food and beverage services and other supporting amenities.

The registration picture is unusually direct at national level. Foreign investment may hold up to 100% ownership in this activity. It is also open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. For a founder, that means the category accommodates both a compact specialist operation and a larger managed water-tourism business without changing the stated national ownership ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The practical reading is clear: foreign participation remains nationally open up to 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium test. The decisive distinction is not a separate Bali ownership cap, but the activity’s higher risk position at the Besar scale.
